title: Recoverability-Controlled Safety Miscalibration in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.22425v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Safety-aligned language models are expected to refuse harmful requests while remaining useful for benign ones. However, because many evaluations score only the final response, they often conflate intent understanding with response-level safety behavior. To address this, we introduce RiskCueBench, a recoverability-controlled benchmark that separates these two stages by first measuring whether a model can successfully recover a high-level intent and then evaluating its safety behavior on the same prompt. RiskCueBench contains 160 latent intents and 640 abstract non-operational surface prompts across eight risk categories. The benchmark covers 25 completed model groups and 32,000 successful model outputs with final rubric-adjudicated labels. When conditioning on pairs where both surface forms are recoverable, we find that increased contextualized specificity induces a shift toward less safe behavior. translated_title: 大型语言模型中可恢复性受控的安全误校准
translated_abstract: 安全对齐的语言模型被期望在拒绝有害请求的同时，对良性请求保持有用性。然而，由于许多评估仅对最终响应进行评分，它们常常将意图理解与响应层面的安全行为混为一谈。为了解决这一问题，我们引入了RiskCueBench，这是一个可恢复性受控的基准测试，通过首先测量模型能否成功恢复高级意图，然后在相同提示上评估其安全行为，从而将这两个阶段分离开来。RiskCueBench包含160个潜在意图和640个抽象的非操作性表层提示，涵盖八个风险类别。该基准测试覆盖25个已完成的模型组和32,000个成功的模型输出，并带有最终由评分标准裁决的标签。在以两种表层形式均可恢复的提示对为条件时，我们发现语境特异性的增加会导致模型行为向较不安全的方向偏移。具体而言，配对自助法估计……
tldr: 提出了可恢复性受控的基准RiskCueBench，将意图理解与响应级安全行为分开评估，发现当提示的语境特异性增加时，大型语言模型在面对可恢复意图的抽象提示时会表现出更不安全的行为。
en_tdlr: We introduce RiskCueBench, a recoverability-controlled benchmark that disentangles intent understanding from response-level safety behavior, revealing that increased contextualized specificity shifts large language models toward less safe behavior on abstract prompts with recoverable intents.
